svg.title: Answering from the index alone
svg.desc: An animation in four steps. An index on players (player_id) finds player 4127 in a leaf page, and an index scan follows the entry's pointer to table page 3 to read the tag. The index is then rebuilt with INCLUDE (tag), so every leaf entry stores the tag too. The visibility map marks page 3 all-visible, so the next lookup returns the tag, Tapir, from the leaf and never reads the table. Then a match changes player 4130's rating, also on page 3. That UPDATE clears the page's bit, and the lookup has to visit page 3 to check that row 4127 is visible.
svg.text: An index-only scan skips the table when the leaf has every column the query reads and the row's page is all-visible.
SELECT tag FROM players WHERE player_id = 4127;
An index scan finds 4127 in a leaf page, then follows its pointer to table page 3 to read the tag.
Rebuilt with INCLUDE (tag), every leaf entry stores the tag too, so the leaf already has the answer.
The visibility map marks page 3 all-visible, so row 4127 is visible to every transaction and the scan skips the table.
After a match, an UPDATE to player 4130's rating clears page 3's bit, so the scan must visit page 3 to check that row 4127 is visible.
